delete.description:
Revoke any key of the caller's project (including agent keys and the caller's own).
Keys of other projects or tenants answer NOT_FOUND.

get.description:
Mailbox change feed after event `since`; resume from `next_since` while `has_more`.
`reset_since` true means the run was reset: resynchronise fully.

schema.title: Response Folders V1 Mailboxes  Mailbox Id  Folders Get

get.description:
List (or with `q`, search subject/body/sender) ordered by (created_at, id).
Follow `next_cursor` until it is null; under a fixed state no item is skipped or repeated.

post.description:
Send a new message. Recipients may be bare addresses or `Name <addr@example.com>`; a
recipient the run does not allow is rejected with EXTERNAL_DELIVERY_BLOCKED (422).

delete.description: Permanently delete a message (to move it to Trash, PATCH `folder: trash`).

patch.description:
Move and/or change labels and flags.

The folder is resolved (404 if unknown) before anything is written. The changes are then
applied as SEPARATE agent writes, in this order: move, labels, flags. Each counts against
the write budget, and if a later step fails (e.g. an unknown flag, or the budget runs out)
the earlier steps stay applied: the error response means "possibly partially applied";
GET the message to see its state.

get.description:
Download one attachment (ids from the message's `attachments`). Served as a download
with its stored media type; never rendered inline. Recorded as a `read`.

200.description: The attachment bytes, always as a download (`Content-Disposition: attachment`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`). Active types (HTML, SVG, XML, scripts, ...) are served as application/octet-stream.

post.description:
Forward a message, attachments included, to `to` (and `cc`); `text` is written above
the forwarded content. Counts as one `forward` operation.

schema.title: Response Get Thread V1 Mailboxes  Mailbox Id  Threads  Thread Id  Get

get.description: Identity of the calling credential (any role).
Schemas and enumerations for the scenario builder and the answer-key editor.

post.description:
Create a project in the caller's TENANT (tenant-wide: any controller key of the tenant
may do this). The response carries the new project's first controller and evaluator keys
(shown once); the caller's own key stays bound to its own project. The very first
tenant/project/keys come from `python -m mailsim.serve bootstrap`.

get.description: The caller's own project only (any other id answers NOT_FOUND).

Runs in the caller's project, newest first (by creation time, then id); filter by
`scenario_key` and/or `status`; follow `next_cursor` until it is null.

schema.title: Response Actions V1 Runs  Run Id  Actions Get

get.description: Recorded actions (newest last) with the interface each came through, for polling.

post.description:
Issue an additional agent key for a run (e.g. after a lost or redacted response, or one
key per interface). Earlier agent keys are NOT revoked: revoke one explicitly with
`DELETE /v1/keys/{key_id}`. Cancelling or completing the run revokes all of them. At most
16 live agent keys per run: beyond that, 409 CONFLICT until one is revoked.

get.description: Trace, raw MIME and attachment blobs; evaluation reports for evaluators only.

schema.title: Response Run Artifacts V1 Runs  Run Id  Artifacts Get

get.description: How an agent connects to this run (endpoints, mailbox, key ids; never key secrets).

post.description:
Make a real call through the chosen interface with the given agent key, server-side.

Always 200 with `ok` and a summary (400 only for a malformed request, 404 for a run outside
the caller's project). A key that is not a live agent key of this run is not tried at all:
ok=false with `details.reason` invalid_key (error_code UNAUTHENTICATED: unknown, revoked,
expired), not_agent_key or other_run (PERMISSION_DENIED; which run is never said). A probe
that is made is recorded in the run's activity like any agent call of that interface. The request body
(and so the key) is never logged, and the key never appears in the result.

`error_code` when `ok` is false:
- REST, MCP (HTTP): the /v1 envelope code (UNAUTHENTICATED, RUN_NOT_ACTIVE,
  PERMISSION_DENIED, ...)
- Gmail: the neutral code in `error.details[0].reason` (UNAUTHENTICATED, RUN_NOT_ACTIVE,
  ...), else `error.status`
- Graph: Graph's own code (InvalidAuthenticationToken; ErrorPreconditionFailed for a run
  that is not running; ErrorAccessDenied ...)
- IMAP: AUTHENTICATIONFAILED; SMTP: AUTHENTICATION_FAILED (credentials refused), or the
  engine's code when it refused a valid key (RUN_NOT_ACTIVE, PERMISSION_DENIED)
- IMAP/SMTP listener not running: LISTENER_DOWN
- gmail / graph / mcp_http not mounted: null (summary "... is not served by this server")
- unexpected failure: INTERNAL

schema.title: Response List Evaluations V1 Runs  Run Id  Evaluations Get

get.description: Download one evaluation's report (JSON, JUnit XML or Markdown).

Event trace in sequence order, optionally filtered by event `type`, `actor` and
`epoch`; follow `next_cursor` (with the same filters) until it is null.
Mailboxes of the run (operator view).

schema.title: Response List Mailboxes V1 Runs  Run Id  Mailboxes Get

post.description:
Inject an inbound message into a simulated mailbox. Nothing ever leaves the sandbox:
the only delivery status is `delivered_to_simulated_mailbox`.

get.description:
Operator read of any mailbox in the run. Unlike the agent mailbox API this is not an
agent action: nothing is recorded and no triggers are armed; finished runs are readable.

Operator download of one attachment of any mailbox in the run (records nothing; works
on finished runs). Always a download: `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `nosniff` and
`Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`, so it is never rendered in the dashboard's origin.

200.description: The attachment bytes, always as a download (`Content-Disposition: attachment`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`). Active types (HTML, SVG, XML, scripts, ...) are served as application/octet-stream.

post.description: Restore the scenario baseline (new epoch). The run is READY again; start it.

get.description: Latest evaluation of the run (spec 7.1 /results).
Canonical mailbox state. `at_sequence` (state as of that event) is evaluator-only.

schema.title: Response State V1 Runs  Run Id  State Get

post.description:
Build an .eml fixture from a composed message (threading headers, attachments).
`date` defaults to the current UTC time, `message_id` to `<uuid@domain of from>`, the path
to `fixtures/<subject slug>-<id prefix>.eml`. CR/LF in any header field: 400.
Summarise an uploaded .eml for display in the form.

Validate an unsaved scenario (schema, references, fixtures). Stores nothing.

Issues carry dotted paths (`scenario.personas.1.email`; `<source>` for text that does not
parse). Malformed requests (both or neither of source/document, bad fixture base64 or
paths) answer 400 INVALID_REQUEST.

get.description:
Scenarios in the caller's project; `tag` matches the latest version's tags, `q` is a
case-insensitive substring of the key or the latest title.

schema.title: Response List Scenarios V1 Scenarios Get

post.description:
Publish a scenario version from YAML/JSON text or a parsed document plus base64
fixtures. Inline evaluation assertions are split off into an evaluator-only answer key.

schema.title: Response List Answer Keys V1 Scenarios  Scenario Key  Answer Keys Get

post.description:
Publish a hidden answer-key version (controller or evaluator). The response is
metadata only.

Schema + leak guard for an unsaved answer key. Stores nothing.

Errors: dotted schema paths (`answer_key.assertions.0.check`), `answer_key.scenario` for a
key of another scenario, `answer_key.scenario_versions` for unknown versions, and
`leak:<scenario version>` when grading prose appears in content the agent can read (the
leaked text is cut to 60 characters). 404 when the scenario does not exist.

get.description: Evaluator-only: the full answer key, for editing.

post.description: Validate schema, references, fixtures and assertions without storing anything.

get.description: A published version's (agent-facing) document and fixtures, for editing or cloning.
Server mode, LLM provider and which interfaces/listeners are up.

post.description: Render a document as YAML (stable key order: the form's order).

Parse YAML/JSON text (safe loader, same limits as publishing). Problems are reported in
`error` (path "line N", 1-based, when the parser knows the line, else "<source>"; the
message has the details), never as HTTP errors.
